chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from Abu Maryam who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The martyr, if he has breath (ramaq), is washed, shrouded, embalmed, and prayer is performed over him; and if he does not have breath, he is buried in his clothes.'

key_terms.صُلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ: Prayer was performed over him (funeral prayer)

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual burial rules for a martyr who dies in battle according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between a martyr who is still alive but dying (retaining 'ramaq') and one who has fully passed away, determining the applicability of full funeral rites. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that the ritual washing (ghusl) and prayer (salat al-janazah) are contingent upon the presence of life, whereas immediate burial in clothes applies only upon complete death. This ruling underscores the physical reality of the martyr's state as a prerequisite for specific burial rituals.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from Abu Maryam who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The martyr, when he was (still with some) breath, would be washed, and enshrouded, and embalmed, and would be prayed Salaat upon; and if he was not with any breath, would be buried in his clothes’.
en.sarwar: 3. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from more than one person from Aban from abu Maryam who has said the following: “

I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘A martyr if found alive is given Ghusl (bath), shroud, hunut and Salah (prayer) is performed for him. If he is found dead he is buried in his clothes.’”
